name: ARC-AGI-2
description: The second iteration of the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for Artificial General Intelligence, designed to test abstract visual pattern recognition and reasoning on novel tasks never seen during training. Puzzles require identifying transformation rules from input-output grid pairs and applying them to new inputs. ARC-AGI-2 is explicitly designed to be 'easy for humans, hard for AI' and measures efficiency (cost per task) alongside accuracy.
reputation: Backed by the ARC Prize Foundation with prize money; designed by Francois Chollet (Keras creator); captures media and research attention as a test of fluid intelligence; humans achieve ~100% while top AI ~84% as of 2025–2026
notes: Tasks are specifically constructed to be novel and non-memorizable, making contamination virtually impossible. Introduces a cost-efficiency dimension rewarding solutions that achieve high accuracy with less compute. Successor to ARC-AGI (2019). Still highly discriminative across frontier models.
